title: Throughput investigation - Standup notes and test log (Nov 5, 2024)
content:
Context: Quick standup/triage for the throughput/latency regression we spotted in prod on 2024-11-03. The regression affected a subset of Hosted API customers and Dedicated pools that use the sequence-length-512 profile. This doc captures notes from the Nov 5 investigation meeting, test runs we executed, preliminary hypotheses, and action items.

Attendees: Priya (owner), Ethan, Marcus, Alyssa, Diego, SRE on-call (J. Park).

Summary:
- Observed regression: ~20-35% increase in p95 token latency for seq=512 workloads on A100 clusters during steady traffic; throughput (tokens/sec) dropped ~18% under our standard batching mix. Regression coincides with deploys on Nov 2 that included the scheduler tweak + kernel selector changes (commit 3f9d2b).
- Reproducible in staging under a synthetic workload that matches real traffic distribution (mix of short-chat + long completion). Not reproduced on H100 instance pool.
- Likely culprits: (1) unexpected kernel selection path for attn that chooses slower fused kernel at certain seq lengths, (2) batching scheduler change that increased head-of-line latency and reduced effective batch density, (3) CUDA driver mismatch on some A100 hosts (driver 535.x vs expected 535.86).

Test runs executed (staging, commit 3f9d2b branch + various rollbacks):
- Baseline (commit 3b2a5d) on A100, seq=512, mix=prod-sample-2024-10-25: p50=12.3ms/token, p95=48.9ms/token, tokens/sec=18.6k. Batch dist: median batch size 12. KV-cache hit simulated: 0.64.
- Regressed (commit 3f9d2b) same config: p50=13.1ms/token, p95=62.8ms/token, tokens/sec=15.2k (drop ~18%). Batch dist: median batch size 9 (fewer coalesced requests).
- Rollback of scheduler-only change (reverted scheduler.go to 3b2a5d) but keep kernel-selector: p95 improved to 51.6ms/token, tokens/sec=17.9k -> suggests scheduler change is primary contributor.
- Kernel-selector-only flip (keep scheduler change, revert kernel selector to previous heuristics): p95=58.3ms/token, tokens/sec=16.1k -> both changes hurt but scheduler has larger signal.
- H100 pool (commit 3f9d2b): no measurable regression (p95 stable ~34ms/token). Suggests kernel/scheduler interaction with A100 microarchitecture or CUDA driver.
- Quick check: machines with driver 535.89 vs 535.86 showed ~6% difference in p95 in isolated tests.

Observed anomalies in traces/logs:
- Trace sampling shows longer queue wait times (queuing inside scheduler) for affected workers; increased precompute waiting and more frequent small batches dispatched (inefficient packing).
- GPU utilization did not spike; instead we saw more idle time between kernel launches.
- Some hosts show a small uptick in memory-steal spikes (OS-level memory reclaim events) coincident with longer p95s.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Scheduler change reduced coalescing window or changed timeout heuristics, causing smaller batches and increased per-request overhead. (High confidence based on rollback tests.)
2) Kernel selector heuristics cause selection of slower kernel variant at sequence boundary when batches are small—amplifies when scheduler yields small batches. (Medium confidence.)
3) CUDA driver mismatch across fleet causes non-deterministic perf differences on A100. (Low->Medium confidence.)

Immediate actions taken during/after the meeting:
- Reverted scheduler tweak on staging and re-ran long-run perf job (k8s-job:perf-run-2024-11-05). Result: p95 nearly restored. Action: create PR to revert scheduler tweak from 3f9d2b in canary branch. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2024-11-06 EOD. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1001 (WIP).
- Instrumented scheduler to emit batch-size distribution histograms and per-worker queue-wait-ms metrics (temporary flag scheduler.debug_batch_metrics=true). Owner: Marcus. ETA: 2024-11-07.
- Added targeted A/B test: route 5% of prod seq=512 traffic to canary with reverted scheduler and extra tracing. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2024-11-07.
- Opened INF-4123 to track fleet driver parity check and a remediation plan to standardize on driver 535.86 across A100 fleet. Owner: SRE. ETA: initial inventory 2024-11-08.
- Kernel selector follow-up: create microbench harness that runs kernel-selection codepath with controlled batch distributions to see at which batch sizes the selector flips. Owner: Alyssa. ETA: 2024-11-12. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987 (reference).

Data dump / commands used (notes-to-self):
- perf harness command (staging): ./tools/perf-run --config=prod-sample-2024-10-25 --seq=512 --duration=30m --pool=a100-staging --commit=3f9d2b
- trace query: ./tools/trace-query --start=2024-11-03T10:00Z --end=2024-11-03T14:00Z --filter=worker:gpu-a100-*
- batch-dist capture: curl -sS http://staging-metrics/metrics?scheduler=hist | jq .batch_size_hist

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why does H100 not show a regression? Is the kernel fallback path different by architecture or is the scheduler heuristics tuned per-GPU? Need to confirm kernel mapping matrix. (Action: Marcus to pull mapping matrix by 2024-11-07.)
- Are there any customer-side patterns (model families, tokenizer differences) that correlate with drop in batch density? (Action: Ethan to query cost/usage logs for customers impacted by INF-4123.)
- Could memory-reclaim spikes be contributing? Need node-level dmesg/syslogs correlated with perf windows. (SRE to investigate.)

Action items (owner | ETA):
- Priya: Open PR to revert scheduler tweak in canary + run 24h smoke. ETA 2024-11-06 EOD.
- Marcus: Add scheduler debug histograms and expose to observability. ETA 2024-11-07.
- Ethan: Start 5% canary traffic routing to reverted scheduler and collect SLO metrics. ETA 2024-11-07.
- Alyssa: Build microbench for kernel-selector to map decision boundaries across batch sizes and seq lengths. ETA 2024-11-12.
- SRE (Diego): Fleet driver inventory and standardization plan, and investigate memory-reclaim events on affected hosts. ETA 2024-11-08 initial report.

Meeting cadence: daily quick sync until mid-next-week or until canary shows stable p95 recovery. Next sync: 2024-11-06 09:30 PT (15 min).

Notes for follow-ups / possible longer-term work:
- Consider adding per-model/route batching policies so high-variance workloads don't collapse batch density for others.
- Add automated canary gate in CI that runs a short perf profile for seq lengths 128/256/512 to catch regressions from scheduler/kernel selector changes before rolling to production.
- Revisit kernel-selection heuristics with upstream vendor (if applicable) for better selection on A100 when batches are small.

Quick raw results table (copied into Confluence later):
- baseline (3b2a5d) | p50 12.3ms | p95 48.9ms | tokens/sec 18.6k | median batch 12
- regressed (3f9d2b) | p50 13.1ms | p95 62.8ms | tokens/sec 15.2k | median batch 9
- revert scheduler | p50 12.5ms | p95 51.6ms | tokens/sec 17.9k | median batch 11

If you have any extra traces, please drop them into the Confluence inbox (confluence:perf/throughput-runbook) or add to the Jira INF-4123.
